notes: Brackets: lines under 86,800 use the tax table (PDF pp.32-38); 86,800 or more use the Tax Rate Schedules (PDF p.39). The schedules are recorded. Each status prints its own schedule; qualifying surviving spouses use the joint one. The schedules were recomputed against p.39's own 'tax on the lower bands' figures (equal, or 1 cent off where the booklet rounds each band first) and against all 3,476 tax table cells under 86,800 at each row's midpoint (at most 54 cents off, at the lowest rows).

Base: Form M1 line 1 starts from federal adjusted gross income. Line 4 standard or itemized deduction, line 5 dependent exemptions, line 6 state income tax refund, line 7 subtractions from Schedule M1M. The booklet prints no personal exemption for the filer or spouse, only the 5,200 dependent exemption.

Age 65 and blind additions: 2,000 single or head of household, 1,550 married or qualifying surviving spouse, printed in Worksheet for Line 4 step 4 and matching the differences in the Standard Deduction Table (PDF p.13). 'Age 65 or older' means born before January 2, 1961 (PDF p.12).

Government pension from another state, New York included: the sources name neither New York nor any other paying state. Such a plan qualifies for the Qualified Public Pension Subtraction only if it allows a similar or reciprocal subtraction or exemption (M1QPEN p.2), and only for service without Social Security credit. paying_states is left out because no state is named; this does not mean every state qualifies. Whether New York meets the test is not stated in the sources. A pension that does not qualify stays in federal AGI with no subtraction found.
Reciprocity on M1M line 18 and PDF p.8 is a different rule: agreements with Michigan and North Dakota for personal service income only, such as wages. It says nothing about pensions.

Own and federal government pensions: only plans listed on M1QPEN p.2 qualify, and the test is service without Social Security credit (basic member), not whether the plan is contributory. CSRS recipients count as basic members and FERS recipients as coordinated. A public pension outside the list, or earned with Social Security credit, stays in federal AGI with no subtraction found; a coordinated member may have the Social Security subtraction instead.

Pension and simplified Social Security step-downs: the record format holds steps, but the validator requires every figure in a record to be printed, and the band edges (for example 86,490 or 88,490) are computed, not printed. The record has no derived_figures. So both stay effect other with the printed formula in as_printed. The projection carries the Social Security bands as steps, with each edge in derived_figures.

rate on an effect other test is off-label: mn_social_security_simplified holds 0.1 (10% per step) and mn_standard_deduction holds 0.03 (first tier only), each explained in as_printed, so the projection can name a record figure.

Social Security: M1M p.3 lets a filer subtract 'the full amount from line 6b' only below the status amounts; above them the subtraction is the greater of step 28 (alternative) and step 29 (simplified), so the entries share a best_of_group. The alternative cap values are the step 23 amounts.

M1M p.3 says full subtraction when AGI is 'below' the status amounts and the worksheet when 'greater'. At exactly the amount the worksheet gives step 3 = 0, so the full amount: effect starts over the amount.
Railroad Retirement Board benefits (line 17) are subtracted with no cap or income test printed; those already in line 6b go through line 12 instead.
Military pensions (line 25): no cap, age or income test printed. Claiming it bars the nonrefundable credit for past military service.

Private pensions, IRA distributions, employer-plan (401(k)) distributions, annuities and Roth conversions: no subtraction, exclusion or special rule found in the booklet. They reach Form M1 through federal AGI (line 1; Line B reports lines 4b and 5b of Form 1040). Not found in the booklet, which is different from the booklet saying there is none; Roth conversions are not mentioned at all. The only general relief these incomes can meet is the Age 65 or Older/Disabled Subtraction, which applies against any income.

Age 65 or Older/Disabled Subtraction (Schedule M1R): three entries, because line 2, line 3 and line 10 differ by branch. It is one amount for the return against any income, not a share of one kind: 9,600, 12,000 or 6,000, less nontaxable Social Security and Railroad Retirement Board benefits, less 50% of AGI over 14,500, 18,000 or 9,000. A household with nontaxable Social Security and Railroad Retirement Board benefits of the line 1 amount or more gets nothing: the worksheet stops at line 8.

mn_disabled_subtraction lists other_income because line 2 takes disability pensions and insurance payments reported on line 1z of Form 1040, the wage line, and no income kind names them. Its married_joint threshold is the 18,000 for both spouses; one spouse is 14,500, as its as_printed says.

Also not in the archive: Schedule M1C (the credit for joint filers with taxable earned income, pension or Social Security income, the long-term care credit, the credit for tax paid to another state, the credit for past military service), Schedule NIIT, Schedule M1MT, Schedule M1LS, Schedule M1NC, Schedule M1SA and Fact Sheet 6, Seniors. Nothing is filled in for them.
Net investment income tax (Schedule NIIT, line 14a): applies to net investment income over 1,000,000 (PDF p.17). Its rate is not printed in the sources, so no surtax entry is recorded.
Capital gains: no separate rate or deduction found in the booklet; empty list. Line 4 of M1M adds back the capital gain portion of a lump-sum distribution elected on federal Form 4972.
Federal conformity: Minnesota rules are generally based on the Internal Revenue Code as amended through May 1, 2023, with Schedule M1NC adjusting for later federal law (PDF p.3).
Income tests use AGI from Form M1 line 1; a partner or shareholder adds pass-through entity taxes first (Adjusted Gross Income Worksheet for PTE Deductions, PDF p.11). Recorded as federal_agi.
Indexing: no document in the archive says anything about adjusting any figure for inflation; PDF p.4 says only that the standard deduction 'increased'. Recorded not_stated.

Other M1M subtractions (K-12 education, 529, charitable contributions over 500, reservation income, active-duty pay, National Guard pay and others) are not recorded as reliefs. Recapture: no rule found that takes back the lower brackets.

indexing.index: Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (BLS), via Minn. Stat. 270C.22; base: statutory year 2019 (first adjusted year 2020); August-to-August change; rounding: nearest $10; an amount ending in $5 rounds up; married-separate bracket is one-half of married-joint

cite.publication: Minn. Stat. 290.06, subd. 2d; 270C.22, subd. 1
cite.section: Minn. Stat. 290.06, subd. 2d; 270C.22, subd. 1: "Subd. 2d. Inflation adjustment of brackets. The commissioner shall annually adjust the minimum and maximum dollar amounts for each rate bracket for which a tax is imposed in subdivision 2c as provided in section 270C.22. The statutory year is taxable year 2019. ... The rate brackets as adjusted must be rounded to the nearest $10 amount. If the rate bracket ends in $5, it must be rounded up to the nearest $10 amount."

indexing.index: Chained CPI-U (BLS), via Minn. Stat. 270C.22; base: statutory year 2023 (adjusts tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2023); rounding: rounded down to the nearest $50; married-separate is one-half of the joint amount

cite.publication: Minn. Stat. 290.0123, subd. 6
cite.section: Minn. Stat. 290.0123, subd. 6: "For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2023, the commissioner must adjust for inflation the standard deduction amounts in subdivision 1, the additional amounts in subdivision 2, the amounts in subdivision 3, and the adjusted gross income amounts in subdivision 5 as provided in section 270C.22. The statutory year is taxable year 2023. The amounts as adjusted must be rounded down to the nearest $50 amount."

cite.publication: Minn. Stat. 290.0802, subd. 2(b)(1) (allowed as a subtraction by 290.0132, subd. 5)
cite.section: Minn. Stat. 290.0802, subd. 2(b)(1) (allowed as a subtraction by 290.0132, subd. 5): "(b)(1) The initial subtraction base amount equals (i) $12,000 for a married taxpayer filing a joint return if a spouse is a qualified individual, (ii) $9,600 for a single taxpayer, and (iii) $6,000 for a married taxpayer filing a separate federal return." | Minn. Stat. 290.0802, subd. 2(b)(2): "(i) $18,000 for a married taxpayer filing a joint return if both spouses are qualified individuals, (ii) $14,500 for a single taxpayer or for a married couple filing a joint return if only one spouse is a qualified individual, and (iii) $9,000 for a married taxpayer filing a separate federal return."

indexing.index: Chained CPI-U (BLS) via Minn. Stat. 270C.22 (simplified Social Security thresholds only); base: statutory year 2023; rounding: nearest $10; $5 rounds up (simplified Social Security thresholds)

cite.publication: Minn. Stat. 290.0132, subd. 26(c), (j)
cite.section: Minn. Stat. 290.0132, subd. 26(c), (j): "(c) ... The phaseout threshold equals: (1) $100,000 for a married taxpayer filing a joint return or surviving spouse; (2) $78,000 for a single or head of household taxpayer ... (j) The commissioner shall adjust the phaseout threshold amounts in paragraph (c), clauses (1) and (2), as provided in section 270C.22. The statutory year is taxable year 2023. The maximum subtraction and threshold amounts as adjusted must be rounded to the nearest $10 amount. If the amount ends in $5, the amount is rounded up to the nearest $10 amount."

cite.publication: Minn. Stat. 290.0132, subd. 26(f), (g), (j)
cite.section: Minn. Stat. 290.0132, subd. 26(f), (g), (j): "(f) For married taxpayers filing a joint return and surviving spouses, the maximum subtraction under paragraph (e) equals $5,840. ... (g) For single or head-of-household taxpayers, the maximum subtraction under paragraph (e) equals $4,560. ... (j) The commissioner shall adjust the phaseout threshold amounts in paragraph (c), clauses (1) and (2), as provided in section 270C.22." | Minn. Stat. 290.0132, subd. 26(f), (g): "(f) ... The maximum subtraction is reduced by 20 percent of provisional income over $88,630. ... (g) ... reduced by 20 percent of provisional income over $69,250."
